titel: Animals and Nature in Tyrol – Alpenzoo, Farms & Co
teaser: From Europe’s highest zoo to cozy children’s farms: Tirol is a paradise for young and old animal lovers.
inhalt:
Tirol offers far more than breathtaking mountain panoramas and top-class ski slopes. The region is also a fascinating destination for anyone looking to experience animals and nature up close. Whether at the **[Alpenzoo Innsbruck](/sehenswuerdigkeiten/alpenzoo-innsbruck)**, on one of the many children’s farms, or on adventures in the wild—here, the whole family will have a blast. Anyone planning a **[family holiday in Tirol](/magazin/familienurlaub-tirol)** should definitely include these animal encounters.

---

### **The Alpenzoo Innsbruck – Home of Alpine Animals**

Founded in 1962, the **[Alpenzoo Innsbruck](/sehenswuerdigkeiten/alpenzoo-innsbruck)** is Europe’s highest zoo, located at 750 meters on the Hungerburg. Over 2,000 animals from around 80 different alpine species live on its expansive grounds. Particularly impressive are the golden eagles, lammergeiers, brown bears, and wolves, which can be observed in spacious, naturalistic enclosures. For children, there’s a large petting zoo with goats, sheep, and donkeys that can be fed and stroked. The Alpenzoo is open year-round and worth a visit in any weather—the **[Innsbruck City Guide](/magazin/innsbruck-city-guide)** even recommends it as a top attraction.

The zoo’s location right next to the Hungerburgbahn cable car station makes it easily accessible from both Innsbruck’s Old Town and the Nordkette. A daily highlight is the bear feeding, where keepers share fascinating facts about the animals. The natural enclosures reflect the diverse alpine habitats—from forests to rocky regions. A visit to the Alpenzoo combines wildlife viewing with breathtaking views of Innsbruck and the surrounding mountains.

---

### **Farm Stay with Petting Zoo and Tiroler Tradition**

A truly special experience for children is staying at one of Tirol’s many **Kinderbauernhöfe** (children’s farms). Here, young guests can watch farmers at work, feed cows, pet goats, and taste fresh milk straight from the farm. Many farms, like the **[Apartbauernhof Valrunzhof](/unterkuenfte/apartbauernhof-valrunzhof)** or the **Bichlhof** in Ebbs, offer family-friendly apartments with on-site farming. This type of holiday blends relaxation in nature with valuable learning experiences for children.

On a farm, kids discover where food comes from and how animals live. Milking cows, collecting eggs in the chicken coop, and feeding calves are experiences that last a lifetime. For parents, too, a farm stay is a welcome break from the hustle of daily life. The warm hospitality of Tiroler farm families and homemade products from their own land make the visit truly unforgettable.

---

### **Nature Adventures in Tirol’s Mountains**

Beyond zoos and farms, Tirol offers countless family-friendly nature experiences. A true highlight is the **Naturerlebnispark** (Nature Experience Park) in the Stubaital, featuring ten hectares of adventure stations, a climbing forest, and a barefoot trail—more details in the article **[Stubaital for Families](/magazin/stubaital-familien)**. The **Grawa-Wasserfall** (waterfall) in the Stubaital is also a worthwhile day trip, easily reached with a short walk. Many regions also offer nature trails where children can playfully explore local wildlife and plants.

Another impressive experience is spotting marmots, chamois, and ibexes in the wild. In the **Hohe Tauern** and **Naturpark Karwendel**, these animals thrive in their natural habitats and are often seen up close on hikes. Many alpine huts welcome visitors with homemade cheese and fresh dairy products. Guided nature walks with rangers provide fascinating insights into alpine wildlife and sharpen your eye for Tirol’s mountain wonders.

---

### **Conclusion – Discovering Animals and Nature in Tirol**

Tirol is the perfect destination for families eager to experience animals and nature in all its forms. The **Alpenzoo Innsbruck**, the many **Kinderbauernhöfe**, and the countless mountain adventures make the region a true paradise for all ages. Whether feeding golden eagles, milking cows on a farm, or watching marmots in the wild—these encounters with alpine wildlife create unforgettable holiday moments. Allow plenty of time and explore the diversity of Tirol’s nature with your whole family.
